topics.name: Safe and Verifiable LLM Agents
topics.summary: Agent security studies combine information-flow taints, tool analysis, formal specifications, runtime topology checks, instruction-priority control, and poisoned-retrieval defenses. Across software, infrastructure, and hardware workflows, explicit constraints make action execution more rejectable and auditable.

topics.name: Governance and Assurance of Autonomous AI
topics.summary: These works measure autonomy, inspect agent evidence, and frame deployment through accountability, cyber resilience, data-quality gates, provenance, and operational stealth. The recurring finding is that reliable oversight must cover runtime behavior and institutional consequences together.

topics.name: Agent Orchestration, Memory, and Workflow Management
topics.summary: Agent infrastructure is organized around routed tools, scoped knowledge surfaces, reusable skills, workflow roles, and actively managed memory. Experiments with enterprise tasks, debate, prompt compression, and long-running systems show that selective retrieval and lifecycle control reduce overhead and improve traceability.

topics.name: Long-Horizon Agent Planning and Control
topics.summary: Long-horizon control combines latent world models, plan-aware representations, solver or game feedback, bounded plan reduction, and state verification. Results across GUI, embodied, and predictive settings indicate that intermediate progress signals help agents sustain coherent action over many steps.

topics.name: Auditable AI Evaluation and Benchmark Validity
topics.summary: Benchmarking work combines data profiling, uncertainty estimates, reference-free checks, provenance tests, and post-task verification. Across language, agent, and clinical settings, scores become more useful when evaluation scope, evidence quality, leakage risk, and transfer assumptions are made explicit.

topics.name: Clinical AI Evaluation and Decision Support
topics.summary: Clinical agent studies evaluate guideline execution, patient-facing workflows, triage, artifact reproducibility, and multimodal world models rather than accuracy alone. Expert criteria and executable checks expose failures in evidence handling, action validation, and clinically meaningful reasoning.

topics.name: Scientific Code Generation and Verification
topics.summary: Generated scientific programs are assessed with executable tests, contracts, hardware feedback, blind retries, and repository-level context. Option pricing, hardware synthesis, clinical coding, repair, and coding-agent studies show that validation and feedback selection matter as much as generation quality.

topics.name: Language Model Training, Adaptation, and Post-Training
topics.summary: Training studies improve language models through data-compute balancing, selective adapters, weak-to-strong distillation, reward shaping, and adaptive rollout budgets. They repeatedly find that supervision placement, initialization geometry, and credit assignment can improve specialization without simply increasing model size.

topics.name: Efficient and Controllable Language Model Inference
topics.summary: Inference methods reduce cost with speculative computation, sparse or optical execution, token compression, localized hidden reasoning, and token-level behavior routing. The common tradeoff is selective computation: latency and memory fall when verification or expert capacity is spent only where uncertainty is high.

topics.name: LLM Reliability, Alignment, and Behavioral Robustness
topics.summary: Behavioral studies probe sycophancy, hallucination mitigation, bit-level attacks, activation steering, adversarial prompts, sampling limits, and preference reversals. Together they show that fluent capability can coexist with unstable calibration, selective bias, or sensitivity to small changes in context and parameters.

topics.name: Mechanistic Interpretability and Neural Representations
topics.summary: Representation studies use probing, spectral comparisons, attribution graphs, intervention, and cross-domain alignment to locate functional structure inside neural systems. Their recurring lesson is that similarity, decodability, weight size, and apparent explanation can diverge from the features that actually drive behavior.

topics.name: Causal and Spurious Feature Analysis
topics.summary: Causal-learning methods test whether models rely on stable mechanisms or environment-specific shortcuts. Response-surface reconstruction, text-treatment masking, in-context subspace analysis, and sensitivity comparisons all aim to improve overlap, effect stability, and transfer beyond the observed setting.

topics.name: Privacy, Backdoors, and Model Integrity
topics.summary: Security analyses cover memorization, hidden skills, poisoned weights, harmful adapters, face de-identification, and privacy-preserving sensing. Extraction tests and weight-level defenses show that deployment artifacts can retain sensitive or malicious behavior even when ordinary outputs look benign.

topics.name: Adversarial Testing of Generative Models
topics.summary: Generative-model defenses and attacks use perturbation, diffusion trajectory steering, forensic residuals, trigger transfer, red-team self-play, and real-data benchmarks. Results across images, video, code competitions, and multimodal systems reveal strong attack transfer but substantial dependence on image quality and detector assumptions.

topics.name: Generative Recommendation and Recommendation Markets
topics.summary: Generative recommenders use semantic item codes, progressive attribute compression, evolutionary indexing, and behavior-aware content generation. Market and serving studies add user agents, retrieval, and rewards, finding that richer item representations improve cold-start and controllability while platform incentives shape exposure.

topics.name: Recommendation Retrieval, Ranking, and Explanation
topics.summary: Recommendation retrieval combines compact language representations, graph-aware ranking, cross-domain transfer, semantic search, and slate optimization. Human studies of explanations and model judges show that ranking quality and explanation framing affect choices differently, so both need separate evaluation.

topics.name: Table Understanding and Semantic Annotation
topics.summary: Table systems improve question answering and schema interpretation through distilled ranking traces, symbolic decision materialization, and explicit column semantics. The shared emphasis is on making multi-table retrieval and labels both more accurate and easier to inspect.

topics.name: Graph Representation Learning and Structured Prediction
topics.summary: Graph methods address heterophily, latent topology, graph explanations, knowledge graphs, and tensor clustering with polynomial filters, conformal sets, sheaf structure, spectral learning, and canonicality analysis. These approaches replace brittle neighborhood assumptions with topology-aware inductive biases.

topics.name: Stochastic and Large-Scale Optimization
topics.summary: Optimization studies analyze Frank-Wolfe clustering, preconditioned linear solves, heavy-tailed stochastic methods, constrained feedback, and variable-size k-means. Convergence proofs and adaptive corrections repeatedly target the gap between idealized feedback and practical numerical data.

topics.name: Bayesian and Uncertainty Modeling
topics.summary: Bayesian neural models use optimizer geometry, heavy-tailed observation assumptions, and probabilistic item-response formulations to improve posterior exploration and benchmark uncertainty. The recurring benefit is better calibrated confidence under misspecification without requiring a major increase in computation.

topics.name: Physics-Informed Scientific Machine Learning
topics.summary: Physics-aware learning combines neural operators, federated PINNs, structured dynamics, and sparse-observation reconstruction for imaging, epidemics, air quality, and engineering simulation. Governing constraints and system structure improve extrapolation, identifiability, or numerical warm starts when measurements are limited.

topics.name: Learning-Augmented Operations Research
topics.summary: Operational systems pair optimization solvers with learned forecasts, Bayesian search, adaptive policies, or decomposition for advertising, inventory, demand sensing, and scheduling. Across these applications, feedback from historical data or solver behavior improves decisions under explicit resource and service constraints.

topics.name: Networking and Experimental Infrastructure
topics.summary: Systems work improves networked ML execution through MoE rate scheduling, wireless foundation representations, and portable experiment backends. The studies connect abstraction choices to measurable utilization, privacy, repeatability, and completion-time improvements.

topics.name: Multimodal Language Models and Video Understanding
topics.summary: Multimodal studies examine frame selection, visual context use, shared continuous-discrete representations, token pruning, visual prompting, and video-data analysis. Benchmarks consistently find that evidence coverage, representation choice, and prompt context determine whether models actually use available visual information.

topics.name: Vision-Language Grounding and Segmentation
topics.summary: Language-guided vision systems use textual inversion, patch-level semantics, semantic maps, clinical descriptions, and counterfactual cues to localize visual evidence. These methods improve recognition of rare, ambiguous, or spatially distributed structures without requiring a heavy alignment stack at deployment.

topics.name: Image and Video Generation and Editing
topics.summary: Generation and editing methods add narrative, physical, identity, luminance, layer, or task-specific controls to diffusion systems. Specialized datasets, lightweight adaptation, and sampling guidance improve local fidelity and temporal consistency beyond generic perceptual scores.

topics.name: Scalable Generative Visual Media
topics.summary: Visual-media systems reduce cost through few-step flow matching, scalable 3D representations, prompt streaming, volumetric rendering, and certified sampling schedules. The recurring goal is preserving usable detail while lowering generation, transmission, or reconstruction expense.

topics.name: Urban and Cross-View Geospatial Perception
topics.summary: Geospatial methods combine semantic maps, geometric correction, reliability-weighted cross-modal features, environmental adaptation, route priors, and cartographic constraints. Urban localization, remote-sensing change detection, travel prediction, and map generalization all benefit from explicitly modeling viewpoint and sensing variation.

topics.name: Hyperspectral and Spectral-Spatial Imaging
topics.summary: Hyperspectral studies restore spatial detail, model illumination and reflectance separately, and use human-guided signatures for material screening. UAV mine detection and spectral-spatial fusion show how physical image structure can reduce review burden and improve material discrimination.

topics.name: Visual Attention and Dynamic Scene Analysis
topics.summary: Dynamic-scene perception uses density-aware saliency, RGB-D video benchmarks, and synchronized eye-tracking or driving data. These datasets show that attention shifts with crowd structure, task context, and observer state rather than following a single fixed visual priority.

topics.name: Robust Visual Perception under Shift
topics.summary: Deployment-oriented vision systems address weather, sensor quality, long-tailed classes, tracking, re-identification, reconstruction, and domain change through calibrated routing, adaptive losses, teacher selection, and test-time adaptation. Their results emphasize that input quality and population shift change the best error tradeoff.

topics.name: Autonomous Driving and Vehicle Dynamics
topics.summary: Autonomous-vehicle studies combine online depth and panoptic fusion with electric freight design and Bayesian Koopman dynamics. The applications target real-time perception, energy-aware convoy operation, and calibrated prediction under changing road conditions.

topics.name: Sleep Physiology and Clinical Time Series
topics.summary: Large polysomnography cohorts and single-channel staging models use temporal fusion, cohort discovery, and longitudinal signals to connect sleep measurements with disease and clinical phenotype. The methods prioritize scalable analysis while retaining local and global rhythm information.

topics.name: Clinical Audio and Speech Biomarkers
topics.summary: Self-supervised speech, breath, EEG, and affective-audio representations support ALS progression, pediatric asthma, emotion, and speech-production analysis. Subject-level aggregation, temporal alignment, and grouped validation recur as safeguards against noisy recordings and patient leakage.

topics.name: Speech Processing and Voice Interfaces
topics.summary: Speech systems address streaming enhancement, speaker-style recovery, forced alignment, federated recognition, music separation metrics, and multilingual codec effects. Compression and causal design support deployment, while evaluation studies show that recording conditions and language choice can alter apparent quality.

topics.name: Cardiovascular AI
topics.summary: Cardiovascular studies pair physician-authored care scenarios with interpretable ECG representations. Benchmark results reveal uneven clinical task performance, while learned cardiac atoms make waveform and phenotype evidence easier to inspect.

topics.name: Multimodal Clinical Reasoning and Forecasting
topics.summary: Clinical forecasting systems combine images, irregular histories, intervention context, temporal graphs, and calibrated regression to model disease trajectories and treatment-dependent outcomes. Their evaluations highlight the need to separate perception errors from evidence synthesis and premature diagnosis.

topics.name: Explainable and Human-Centered Healthcare AI
topics.summary: Healthcare explainability work combines federated prediction with interviews and user-centered elicitation to study what explanations patients and caregivers can use. The recurring concern is that transparency must reflect clinical decisions and human needs, not merely expose model internals.

topics.name: AI for Mental Health Assessment
topics.summary: Mental-health systems use multimodal benchmarks, CBT-oriented language tasks, cognitive-distortion labels, and structured summaries for depression, anxiety, stress, and therapy training. Human review remains central because calibration, simulation fidelity, and supportive wording affect safety as much as classification accuracy.

topics.name: Medical Image Representation and Tissue Structure
topics.summary: Biomedical imaging methods learn structure from CT, histopathology, PET, MRI, photoacoustic, and stain-transfer data using foundation embeddings, temporal or graph organization, metric learning, and reconstruction. Dataset-specific geometry and multiscale tissue context repeatedly improve transfer and diagnostic sensitivity.

topics.name: Label-Efficient Medical Vision
topics.summary: Sparse-label medical vision uses scribbles, pseudo-label propagation, equivariance, and structural priors to segment or detect rare findings. These approaches show that task-specific inductive bias can compensate for missing dense annotations and unstable class frequencies.

topics.name: Human Activity and Body Measurement
topics.summary: Body-centered vision systems estimate impact events, stature, body composition, and exposed skin from unconstrained imagery or joint sequences. Temporal skeleton modeling and biomechanical or anatomical cues improve robustness when pose, visibility, and background vary.

topics.name: Robot Navigation and Multi-Agent Autonomy
topics.summary: Navigation research combines minimal-sensor exploration, photorealistic social simulation, cooperative UAV policies, marine autonomy, heterogeneous perception, and causal multi-agent world models. Safety, decentralized execution, privacy, and transfer across layouts or platforms are recurring evaluation criteria.

topics.name: Robot Manipulation and Embodied Learning
topics.summary: Manipulation systems learn from demonstrations and multimodal feedback while using 3D object structure, action tokens, temporal views, tactile or spectral cues, and hardware-aware execution. Results across suturing, catheter work, construction, and general grasping emphasize transfer and closed-loop correction.

topics.name: Robot Policy Transfer and Structured Control
topics.summary: Robot-control studies inject actuator or rigid-body dynamics, privileged latent guidance, distribution-aware optimization, and calibration into policy learning. Cross-generation and quadrotor experiments show that transfer succeeds when the receiving hardware or controller has enough task competence and matching structure.

topics.name: Motion Understanding, Generation, and Style Transfer
topics.summary: Motion methods represent atomic actions, part-local edits, hand coordination, EMG movement classes, and human-to-quadruped behavior with structured tokens or disentangled factors. The shared aim is controllable temporal variation without unintended changes to unrelated body parts or action phases.

topics.name: Social Systems, Coordination, and Inequality
topics.summary: Agent-based models, human-robot interaction studies, negotiation systems, team experiments, and immersive community research examine how incentives, trust, status, attention, and hidden objectives alter cooperation. Outcomes depend strongly on interaction structure and perceived legitimacy, not only on individual policy quality.

topics.name: Language Use and Cognitive Modeling
topics.summary: Language studies measure contextual persistence, code-switched entrainment, language-area evidence, synthetic poetry, radio corpora, turn-taking, and convergence between model and human cognition. The recurring theme is that sequence behavior reflects both reusable linguistic structure and interaction-specific adaptation.

topics.name: Human-Computer Interaction for Data Work
topics.summary: HCI studies examine serialization, data wrangling, chart refinement, design reasoning, and engineering education through controlled tasks and psychological measures. Success depends on abstraction, documentation, inferred structure, and user needs rather than visual structure or task accuracy alone.

topics.name: LLM-Simulated Human Behavior
topics.summary: Psychometric evaluations compare prompted synthetic respondents with human surveys across domains and item difficulties. Cognitive-profile prompts can improve aggregate calibration, but demographic prompting may exaggerate group differences, making real-response validation essential before operational use.

topics.name: Human Evaluation of AI-Assisted Knowledge Work
topics.summary: Human studies compare AI and expert outputs in scientific planning, literature support, coding artifacts, preprint impact, and chess analysis. They find that speed and apparent quality depend on task and evaluator, with systematic preference effects and domain-specific verification needs.

topics.name: Online Content Moderation and Counterspeech
topics.summary: Moderation research evaluates filter placement, response rewriting, misinformation exposure, user history, and contextual counterspeech through platform data and user studies. Interventions gain utility when they preserve benign intent and audience context, although stronger filtering can reduce coverage.

topics.name: GenAI Platforms and Content Economics
topics.summary: Platform studies model attribution competition and advertising sidecars around generated answers. Their analyses show that revenue mechanisms, disclosure, and credit assignment can improve monetization while creating tradeoffs in welfare, visibility, and incentives for upstream model providers.

topics.name: LLM-Assisted Quantum Computing
topics.summary: Language-model agents help formulate quantum code, fuzz libraries, evaluate circuits, and diagnose hardware while relying on physically grounded checks. The studies report faster exploration but also show that expert validation is needed when observables or hardware explanations are ambiguous.

topics.name: Failure Prognostics and Root-Cause Analysis
topics.summary: Operational prognostics use multivariate histories, federated survival models, intent-failure prediction, and remaining-useful-life estimates to move beyond reactive alarms. The methods distinguish upstream causes from symptoms while protecting site-specific sensor data.

topics.name: Climate Variability and Extreme-Heat Risk
topics.summary: European climate studies relate warming tails and forecast skill to persistent ocean-linked states and regional memory. Filtered spatial analyses and out-of-sample modeling suggest that slow circulation changes can alter both warming gradients and extreme-heat risk.

topics.name: Offline Reinforcement Learning under Data Shift
topics.summary: Offline reinforcement-learning methods handle transition mismatch and unobserved actions with shift-aware identification, proxy transitions, and robust policy evaluation. Their guarantees and estimators target settings where logged trajectories do not faithfully describe the deployment environment.

topics.name: Computational Molecular Design
topics.summary: Molecular-learning studies model peptide interfaces, drug representations, antimicrobial activity, electrolyte structure, and infrared molecular composition with diffusion, multimodal, and physics-aware representations. The applications emphasize transfer across chemical space and useful uncertainty for discovery or safety screening.

topics.name: Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning
topics.summary: Theory-oriented work studies active subspaces, depth separation, normalizing flows, operator stability, implicit bias, random fields, geometric lengths, and matrix factorization. These analyses provide structural explanations for expressivity, conditioning, sampling, and generalization in neural and generative models.

topics.name: Federated and Decentralized Learning
topics.summary: Collaborative-learning methods address partition heterogeneity, corrupted updates, missing features, and privacy without pooling raw data. Fisher regularization, selective aggregation, and distributed inference improve robustness while preserving local measurements and site autonomy.
